== Research Notes ==

A possible identification concerns Sarah McCaughern. The 1911 Gortereghy census browse records Sarah McCaughern, aged 82, as head of household with Matilda Mulholland, 52, and Caroline McCaughern, 47, recorded as daughters; Sara Jane McCaughern, 45, and Jas Alex McCaughern, 43, are also listed as children, with Geo Mulholland, 14, as grandson. It confirms a substantial McCaughern household in the same townland as the Elder and Glasgow-associated records, but it does not identify Sarah's husband, parents or relationship to Mary Glasgow.<ref>1911 Gortereghy, Sarah McCaughern household; [https://api-census.nationalarchives.ie/census/image/nai001390134.pdf record].</ref> The identification remains uncertain.

A possible identification concerns Sarah McCaughern. The original 1901 and 1911 returns establish continuity of Sarah McCaughern’s Gortereghy family. Sarah was a Derry-born widow aged 72/82; Caroline, Sarah J/Sara Jane, James A/Jas Alex, Matilda and grandson George occur in both returns. Elizabeth, 32, is also a daughter in 1901. Sarah [[Dysart-1893]], married in 1851 to Gortereghy farmer John McCaughern, remains the strongest mother identity, but neither census names her deceased husband or maiden surname.<ref>1901 Gortereghy, Sarah McCaughern household; [https://api-census.nationalarchives.ie/census/image/nai000298441.pdf record]; 1911 Gortereghy, Sarah McCaughern household; [https://api-census.nationalarchives.ie/census/image/nai001390134.pdf record]; Rasharkin Presbyterian civil marriage register 1851; [https://www.irishgenealogy.ie/files/civil/marriage_returns/marriages_1851/09402/5405894.pdf record].</ref> The identification remains uncertain.
